documents.title: History and Physical - Admission
lines: HPI:
77 yo female with known HFrEF presents to ED with 1 week of progressive dyspnea on exertion and leg swelling.
Pt reports she can no longer walk to the mailbox without stopping; sleeps in recliner x3 nights due to orthopnea.
Two-pillow orthopnea at baseline, now four pillows or recliner. Reports 1 episode of PND two nights ago.
Cardiology clinic doubled home furosemide to 80 mg twice daily 5 days ago; patient reports adherence; weight gain of 4.5 kg over that period with worsening leg swelling.
Daughter confirms pt has been taking all pills from the weekly box; no missed doses noted.
Admits to canned soup and deli meat over the past week at a family gathering.
Denies chest pain, palpitations, syncope, fever, cough with sputum, hemoptysis.
No recent travel, no calf pain.
Abdominal fullness and early satiety for 4 days.
PMH:
HFrEF, last documented EF 35%
Permanent atrial fibrillation on anticoagulation
HTN
CKD - stage not documented in available record
Type 2 DM, diet controlled
Osteoarthritis, bilateral knees
Home Medications:
furosemide 80 mg PO BID (recently doubled)
carvedilol 6.25 mg PO BID
sacubitril-valsartan 24-26 mg PO BID
spironolactone 12.5 mg PO daily
apixaban 5 mg PO BID
atorvastatin 40 mg PO daily
acetaminophen 650 mg PO q8h prn knee pain
Allergies: sulfa - rash
Social: lives with daughter, uses cane indoors, walker outside. Former smoker, quit >30 yrs ago. No alcohol.
ROS: as per HPI, otherwise negative in 10 systems.
Physical Exam:
Vitals at triage 19:42 - T 36.7, HR 96 irregular, BP 148/84, RR 22, SpO2 92% on RA at triage; placed on 2L NC for comfort.
Gen: elderly female, mildly tachypneic at rest, speaking in full sentences.
HEENT: JVD to angle of jaw at 45 degrees.
Cardiac: irregularly irregular, S3 present, no murmur appreciated, PMI displaced laterally.
Lungs: bibasilar crackles to mid lung fields posteriorly, no wheeze.
Abd: soft, mildly distended, liver edge 3 cm below costal margin, no tenderness.
Ext: 3+ pitting edema to mid thigh bilaterally, warm, no cords.
Skin: chronic venous stasis changes both shins, no ulceration.
Neuro: alert, oriented x3, no focal deficit.
Labs:
Creatinine 1.4 mg/dL on arrival; no baseline available in the record.
WBC 7.2, Hgb 11.4, Plt 212
Troponin 0.03, flat on repeat at 02:10
TSH 2.1, albumin 3.4, AST 28, ALT 22, total bili 1.1
EKG: atrial fibrillation at 98, LVH with repolarization changes, no acute ischemic change.
Assessment/Plan:
1. Acute decompensated heart failure, volume overloaded, likely dietary sodium plus progression despite outpatient uptitration.
Furosemide 80 mg IV given in the ED, repeated at 80 mg IV every 12 hours.
Strict I/O, daily standing weights, foley deferred, urinal/bedside commode.
2L fluid restriction, 2 g sodium diet.
Daily BMP, replace K to keep >4.0.
2. CKD - creatinine 1.4 on arrival, monitor closely with diuresis, hold sacubitril-valsartan for now.
3. Permanent AF - continue apixaban, rate controlled, continue carvedilol at home dose.
4. Hypoxia - on 2L NC, wean as tolerated, target SpO2 >92%.
5. DM2 - hold nothing, CBG monitoring q6h.
DVT ppx: therapeutic apixaban.
Discussed plan with pt and daughter at bedside. Cardiology consulted, will see in AM.

documents.title: Progress Note - HD2 Morning
lines: Subjective:
Pt states breathing is somewhat better, slept 4 hrs supine on one pillow overnight. Still short of breath with walking to bathroom.
No chest pain, no palpitations.
Overnight events: none. Weaned off nasal cannula at 06:15 and stable on room air since - SpO2 94% on RA at 07:30.
Intake/Output: UOP 460 mL over the last 24 hrs despite IV bolus dosing. Intake 1150 mL.
Weight 84.1 kg, up 0.2 kg from admission weight.
Exam:
Vitals - T 36.5, HR 88 irreg, BP 132/76, RR 20, SpO2 94% RA
Gen: more comfortable, no accessory muscle use
Cardiac: irregularly irregular, S3 still present
Lungs: crackles now lower third bilaterally
Abd: soft, less distended
Ext: 3+ edema to thighs, unchanged
Labs: Na 133, K 3.5, BUN 36, creatinine 1.5, Mg 1.8
Assessment/Plan:
1. Acute decompensated HF - inadequate diuretic response to intermittent bolus dosing.
Converted to furosemide infusion at 10 mg/hr on hospital day 2 for urine output under 500 mL.
Goal net negative 1.5 to 2 L/day. Reassess in 6 hrs, will add metolazone if response remains poor.
KCl 40 mEq PO x2 doses, magnesium 2 g IV.
Repeat BMP this afternoon and again in AM.
2. Renal - creatinine trending 1.4 to 1.5, expected with diuresis, continue to hold sacubitril-valsartan.
3. AF - rate controlled, continue carvedilol and apixaban.
4. Respiratory - off supplemental O2, no further O2 needed, continue to monitor with ambulation.
5. Mobility - PT consult for gait assessment, up with assist.
Cardiology saw pt, agrees with infusion strategy, recommends TTE this admission.
Continue 2 g sodium diet and 2 L fluid restriction. Family updated by phone at 10:20.

documents.title: Progress Note - HD5
lines: Subjective:
Pt feels markedly improved. Walked hallway x2 with walker and PT yesterday without dyspnea. Sleeping flat on one pillow.
Appetite returning, no abdominal fullness. No orthopnea, no PND overnight.
I/O: net negative 1.9 L over last 24 hrs. Cumulative net negative 7.8 L since admission.
Weight 77.9 kg, down 6.2 kg from admission.
Exam:
Vitals - T 36.6, HR 76 irreg, BP 118/68, RR 16, SpO2 96% RA
Gen: comfortable, sitting up in chair
HEENT: JVD now ~6 cm at 45 degrees
Cardiac: irregularly irregular, S3 no longer appreciated
Lungs: clear to auscultation bilaterally
Abd: soft, nondistended, liver edge no longer palpable
Ext: trace to 1+ edema at ankles only
Labs: Na 136, K 4.1, BUN 34, creatinine 1.5, Mg 2.0
TTE HD3: EF 30-35%, moderate MR, moderately dilated LA, RV function mildly reduced.
Assessment/Plan:
1. Acute decompensated HF - near euvolemic. Furosemide infusion stopped at 08:00, transition to furosemide 80 mg IV x1 then oral dosing.
Plan oral regimen furosemide 80 mg PO BID with close outpatient follow up.
Daily weights continue, document dry weight prior to discharge.
2. Renal - creatinine stable at 1.5 on stable diuresis, tolerate. Restart sacubitril-valsartan 24-26 mg PO BID today, recheck BMP in AM.
3. AF - rate controlled 70s-80s, continue apixaban 5 mg BID and carvedilol.
4. GDMT - spironolactone 12.5 mg resumed, K 4.1, monitor.
5. Dispo - likely home HD6 with daughter. PT cleared with walker. HF teaching started by RN: daily weights, salt, when to call.
Discussed discharge timeline with pt and daughter at 11:40.

documents.title: Discharge Summary
lines: Admission diagnosis: Acute decompensated heart failure (CHF exacerbation)
Discharge diagnosis: Acute on chronic HFrEF, euvolemic at discharge; CKD; permanent atrial fibrillation
Length of stay: HD1 to HD6
Hospital Course:
77 yo female with HFrEF presented with 1 week of progressive dyspnea, orthopnea and leg swelling.
Cardiology clinic doubled home furosemide to 80 mg twice daily 5 days ago; patient reports adherence; weight gain of 4.5 kg over that period with worsening leg swelling.
SpO2 92% on RA at triage; placed on 2L NC for comfort and weaned to RA by the next morning. Remained on room air thereafter.
Furosemide 80 mg IV given in the ED, repeated at 80 mg IV every 12 hours; converted to furosemide infusion at 10 mg/hr on hospital day 2 for urine output under 500 mL.
Brisk diuresis followed on infusion with net negative 1.5 to 2 L daily. Infusion stopped HD5 and pt transitioned to oral diuretic.
Creatinine 1.4 mg/dL on arrival; no baseline available in the record. Peaked at 1.5 and remained stable through discharge.
Sacubitril-valsartan held during active diuresis, resumed HD5 at 24-26 mg PO BID and tolerated.
Potassium and magnesium repleted as needed; K 4.2 and creatinine 1.5 on day of discharge.
TTE HD3: EF 30-35%, moderate MR, moderately dilated LA, mildly reduced RV function.
Troponin flat, EKG showed atrial fibrillation without ischemic change.
Total net fluid removal approximately 9.4 L. Discharge weight 77.4 kg, down 6.7 kg from admission.
At discharge pt ambulating hallway with walker, lungs clear, trace ankle edema, no orthopnea.
Discharge Medications:
furosemide 80 mg PO BID
carvedilol 6.25 mg PO BID
sacubitril-valsartan 24-26 mg PO BID
spironolactone 12.5 mg PO daily
apixaban 5 mg PO BID
atorvastatin 40 mg PO daily
acetaminophen 650 mg PO q8h prn
Allergies: sulfa - rash
Discharge instructions:
2 g sodium diet, 2 L daily fluid restriction.
Weigh daily each morning after voiding, before breakfast; call if up 1 kg in a day or 2 kg in 3 days.
Call for worsening dyspnea, orthopnea, increased leg swelling, or lightheadedness.
Follow up: cardiology clinic in 5 to 7 days with BMP; primary care in 2 weeks.
Home health RN arranged for weight and medication review twice weekly.
Discharged home with daughter at 14:20 on HD6, stable, no supplemental oxygen required.
Condition at discharge: stable, improved.
